questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option for the given blank.

The team _____ children on proper safety procedures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **educated**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the **past tense**, so the correct form of the verb should also be in the past tense.
 
• Among the given options, the past tense form of the verb is **'educated'**.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *The team educated children on proper safety procedures*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• **educate **- This is the base form of the verb. It is incorrect because it does not match the past tense context implied by the rest of the sentence.
 
• **education **- This is a noun, not a verb, and does not fit grammatically in the structure of the sentence which requires a verb.
 
• **educating **- This is the present participle form of the verb. It is inappropriate here because the sentence needs a past tense verb to indicate that the action has already been completed.

questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error’.

In the afternoon we walk in the Parks; / and I wondered who shod all the horses there, / and wished Joe did.

options.text: In the afternoon we walk in the Parks;
and I wondered who shod all the horses there,

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **In the afternoon we walk in the Parks;**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence has mixed tenses, which is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the verbs in the first and third parts are in the past tense (wondered, wished).
 
• The verb in the second part, "walk," should also be in the past tense to maintain consistency.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be 'walked' instead of 'walk'.

Correct sentence: *In the afternoon we walked in the Parks; and I wondered who shod all the horses there, and wished Joe did.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Verb tense consistency means maintaining the same tense throughout the sentence.
 
• Mixing present and past tenses inappropriately can confuse the reader.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• Incorrect: *She **walks** into the room and **sat** down.*
 
• Correct: *She **walked** into the room and **sat** down.*

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I want to __loose weight,__ yet I eat chocolate daily.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **lose weight**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word 'loose' is incorrect in this context as it means *not tight or free from constraints*.
 
• The appropriate word in the context is 'lose', which means *to have less of something, especially weight*.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be 'lose weight' instead of 'loose weight.'

Correct sentence: *I want to lose weight, yet I eat chocolate daily*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Loose vs. Lose:

 
 
• Loose: *not firmly or tightly fixed in place*.

 
 
• ***Example:** The shirt is loose*.
 
 
 
• Lose: *become unable to find* or *fail to keep*.
 
 
• ***Example:** I want to lose weight*.
 
 
 
 
 
• Common mistake: Many people confuse 'loose' with 'lose' due to the similarity in spelling and pronunciation.
